record.paper_title: Open problems in stochastic reinforcement models
record.context_brief: Whisker support threshold for strong WARM
record.original_question: For finite-graph WARMs with strong reinforcement alpha > 1 and uniform firing rates p(v)=1, the source states that for alpha > 25 each connected component of the limiting support is a whisker, meaning a tree of diameter at most 3. Can the lower bound alpha > 25 be improved, and what is the sharp threshold for this whisker property?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 13 Improve the lower bound α > 25 for which (when p(v) ≡ 1) every connected component is a whisker.
a whisker, a tree graph of diameter at most 3

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite connected graph. A Weighted Attachment Reinforcement Model (WARM) on $G$ with reinforcement exponent $\alpha>1$ and firing rates $p(v)=1$ for all $v\in V$ is defined as follows. At each vertex $v\in V$ one has an independent rate-$1$ Poisson clock; when the clock at $v$ rings, an incident edge $e\ni v$ is selected with probability proportional to $W_e(t)^\alpha$, and its weight is increased by $1$. Here $W_e(t)$ denotes the cumulative weight of edge $e$ at time $t$ (starting from $W_e(0)=1$, say).

Let $x_e=\lim_{t\to\infty} W_e(t)/t\in[0,\infty)$ (these limits exist almost surely under suitable conditions), and define the limiting support
$$S=\{e\in E:\ x_e>0\}.$$
Call a finite tree a "whisker" if its diameter is at most $3$.

Known fact. There exists a constant $\alpha_0$ such that for all $\alpha>\alpha_0$, every connected component of the subgraph $(V,S)$ is, almost surely, a whisker. The value $\alpha_0=25$ is known to suffice.

Problem. Determine the sharp threshold
$$\alpha^* := \inf\{\alpha>1:\ \text{for every finite graph }G\text{ and every }\alpha'>\alpha,\ \text{a.s. every connected component of the limiting support is a whisker}\}.$$
In particular, improve the bound $\alpha^*\le 25$.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches turn up the known result that for finite graphs with uniform firing rates the limiting support consists of whisker components when α > 25 (proved in work on the WARM whisker conjecture by Holmes–Kleptsyn and related papers on infinite WARM graphs in the strong reinforcement regime). No source claims an improved explicit threshold below 25 or identifies the sharp value, so the question of improving the bound and finding the sharp threshold appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Proof of the WARM whisker conjecture for neuronal connections
status_evidence.snippet: when α > 25, [equilibria are supported] on spanning whisker forests
status_evidence.claim: The threshold α > 25 for the whisker property is the known sufficient bound; no improved value is stated.

status_evidence.title: Infinite WARM graphs III: strong reinforcement regime
status_evidence.snippet: strong reinforcement regime; components are trees of diameter at most 3 when α is sufficiently large
status_evidence.claim: Recent works continue to use a 'sufficiently large α' formulation rather than a sharper explicit constant.

status_evidence.title: Absence of WARM percolation in the very strong reinforcement regime
status_evidence.snippet: for α ≫ 1 the random subgraph of edges does not percolate
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature addresses related strong-reinforcement questions without giving the sharp whisker threshold.
